story_facts_verified.project: The Estrella, a mixed-use tower proposed for 175-199 E. Rich St. in downtown Columbus (Red Brick / Fourth Street district, just east of Columbus Commons). Developer Bluestone Brothers; architect Berardi+Partners.
story_facts_verified.current_filing: A Certificate of Appropriateness application, COA2601058, was filed September 30, 2026 describing a 25-story building with 296 apartments, roughly 30,000 sq ft of ground-floor commercial space for a fresh-food grocery, and 327 parking spaces (Hoodline, Oct. 2, 2026). The City of Columbus Downtown Commission page confirms an October 27, 2026 meeting (8:30 a.m.) and a September 30, 2026 application deadline for that agenda. The October 27 review is conceptual (non-binding), not an approval or a construction authorization.
story_facts_verified.state_award: Ohio Department of Development 2025 TMUD award-descriptions record (released with Gov. DeWine's Jan. 27, 2025 announcement of $2 billion in TMUD-supported investment): The Estrella (Franklin County) -- Total Development Cost $122,605,000; Total Tax Credit $4,500,000; 175-199 Rich St., a 24-story, 503,103-square-foot mixed-use tower; fresh-food grocery in a food desert; approximately 1,239 construction jobs and 808 permanent jobs. Corroborated by ABC6/FOX28 (Jan. 28, 2025).
story_facts_verified.height_history: 19 stories (first pitched 2023) -> 24 stories (the version the state backed in Jan. 2025 and the commission last reviewed) -> 25 stories (the Sept. 30, 2026 COA filing). The 2023 and current-filing heights are from news reporting (Hoodline); the 24-story figure is from the primary state record.
story_facts_verified.original_contributions: Direct reading and text-extraction of the primary Ohio TMUD award-descriptions PDF; a reconciled height-and-spec timeline (19 -> 24 -> 25 stories; 290 -> 296 units) built across the state record, the city meeting record, and the current filing; identification that the developer's own first-party project page still shows the earlier 24-story/290-unit/~18,000-sq-ft design, lagging the Sept. 30 filing; and an original CREN height chart from the verified records.
story_facts_verified.limitations_stated: The 25-story/296-unit figures come from the Sept. 30 COA filing as reported by Hoodline; CREN could not open the COA2601058 application file through the city's Citizens Access Portal this run, and the developer's public page still lists the 24-story/290-unit design. The Oct. 27 review is conceptual and binds nothing. The TMUD credit is earned against taxes over time, not paid up front, and state awards can lapse if a project stalls. No grocery operator is named in the public record; no construction timeline is established.
